entries.title: CKD defined by eGFR <60 or markers of damage for ≥3 months
entries.snippet: CKD is defined as abnormalities of kidney structure or function present for >3 months, with implications for health. Markers include albuminuria (ACR ≥30 mg/g), urine sediment abnormalities, electrolyte abnormalities from tubular disorders, histologic or imaging abnormalities, history of kidney transplantation, or eGFR <60 mL/min/1.73 m². (Paraphrased.)
entries.source_doc: KDIGO 2024 Clinical Practice Guideline for the Evaluation and Management of CKD
entries.applies_when: any adult with abnormal eGFR or albuminuria
entries.demo_relevance: Kowalski eGFR 62 — does NOT meet CKD definition by eGFR alone; needs ACR + chronicity confirmation. Often loosely called 'stage 2' but CKD requires markers of damage if eGFR ≥60.

entries.title: CGA staging: cause, GFR category (G1–G5), albuminuria category (A1–A3)
entries.snippet: CKD should be classified based on Cause, GFR category (G1 ≥90; G2 60–89; G3a 45–59; G3b 30–44; G4 15–29; G5 <15), and Albuminuria category (A1 <30; A2 30–300; A3 >300 mg/g). Risk of progression and adverse outcomes increases with lower GFR and higher albuminuria. (Paraphrased.)
entries.source_doc: KDIGO 2024 Clinical Practice Guideline for the Evaluation and Management of CKD
entries.demo_relevance: Kowalski eGFR 62 = G2; ACR is needed to assign A1/A2/A3 and finalize CGA stage.

entries.title: Confirm CKD with repeat testing over ≥3 months
entries.snippet: Following incidental detection of elevated urinary albumin-to-creatinine ratio, hematuria, or low eGFR, tests should be repeated to confirm the presence of CKD and establish chronicity (≥3 months).
entries.source_doc: KDIGO 2024 Clinical Practice Guideline for the Evaluation and Management of CKD
entries.demo_relevance: Kowalski eGFR 62 needs repeat eGFR + ACR before being labelled CKD.

entries.title: Target SBP <120 mmHg in CKD when tolerated; RAAS blockade for albuminuria
entries.snippet: We suggest targeting a systolic blood pressure of <120 mmHg, when tolerated, using standardized office BP measurement in adults with high BP and CKD. We recommend starting RAS inhibitors (ACEi or ARB) for people with high BP, CKD, and severely increased albuminuria (G1–G4, A3) without diabetes, and we recommend starting RAS inhibitors for people with high BP, CKD, and moderately-to-severely increased albuminuria (G1–G4, A2 and A3) with diabetes. (Paraphrased; aligns with KDIGO 2021 BP guideline carried into 2024 CKD guideline.)
entries.applies_when: adult with CKD and hypertension; albuminuria modifies RAASi indication
entries.demo_relevance: Kowalski (eGFR 62, K 3.3) — if albuminuric, RAASi indicated; low K is a relative caution and requires monitoring.

entries.title: When to refer to nephrology
entries.snippet: Refer adults with CKD to specialist kidney care services for: eGFR <30 mL/min/1.73 m² (G4–G5), severely increased albuminuria (ACR ≥300 mg/g, A3), persistent hematuria with albuminuria, rapid progression of CKD, refractory hypertension, recurrent or extensive nephrolithiasis, hereditary kidney disease, or persistent abnormalities of serum potassium. (Paraphrased.)
entries.source_doc: KDIGO 2024 Clinical Practice Guideline for the Evaluation and Management of CKD
entries.applies_when: any patient with established CKD evaluated for specialist referral
entries.demo_relevance: Kowalski eGFR 62 — not yet a referral trigger by GFR alone; depends on ACR and progression rate.

entries.title: Monitoring frequency by risk category
entries.snippet: Frequency of eGFR and ACR monitoring should be guided by the heat-map of risk: low risk at least annually; moderately increased risk every 6–12 months; high risk every 3–6 months; very high risk every 1–3 months. (Paraphrased.)
entries.source_doc: KDIGO 2024 Clinical Practice Guideline for the Evaluation and Management of CKD
entries.applies_when: any patient at risk for or with CKD
entries.demo_relevance: Kowalski G2 + likely metabolic risk — at minimum annual ACR/eGFR; if A2/A3 found, every 6 months.
